COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS

Anuj Agarwal
 --Petitioner
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
 --Respondent
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.
Hon'ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel for the
petitioners.
2. Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned Additional Chief
Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/
respondent no. 1.
3. Ms. Shirin Khajuria, learned Senior Counsel
assisted by Mr. Piyush Garg and Mr. Dharmendra
Barthwal, learned counsel for respondent no. 2.
4. Mr. Abhishek Singh, Ms. Amrita Sharma & Ms.
Priyanka Agarwal, learned counsel for respondent nos.
3, 19, 27 & 28.
5. Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior Counsel
assisted by Mr. C.S. Dalakoti, learned counsel for
respondent nos. 3 to 7, 14, 15, 17, 18 & 19.
6. In the present Writ Petition, the petitioners have
called in question the seniority list of Assistant
Engineers, issued by the Uttarakhand Power
Corporation Ltd. vide Office Memorandum dated
04.06.2025.
7. The submission of Shri Shobhit Saharia, Advocate
appearing on behalf of the petitioners, is that the
present seniority list is in teeth of the directions issued
by this Court, vide judgment dated 27.06.2024 passed
in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 579/2017 and other

connected matters.
8. The submission of learned counsel for the
petitioners is that the respondents, on basis of the
impugned seniority list, are in a hurry to hold DPC and
make promotions on the post of Executive Engineers,
which would cause serious prejudice to the petitioners.
9. We observe that some of the private
respondents, namely respondent nos. 3 to 7, 14, 15,
17, 18, 19, 27 & 28 are duly represented.
10. Having regard to the nature of the controversy,
we permit the petitioners to serve the remaining
private respondents by speed post, by taking steps
within three days. In addition, these respondents
would also be served by the Uttarakhand Power
Corporation Ltd., as these private respondents are
under its employment.
11. Learned Senior Counsel for the respondent-Corporation states that she has instructions that the
Corporation would not hold DPC for two weeks.
12. Having regard to the above, let the instant
matter be listed on 26.02.2026.
13. In the meantime, it shall be open to the parties
to exchange affidavits.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
 16.02.2026 16.02.2026
Rahul
